Content marketing is the process of creating and sharing useful content to attract potential customers. Instead of directly asking people to buy, you give them information that helps them solve a problem or make a decision. Blog posts, videos, social media posts, emails, guides, case studies, and checklists are common types of content marketing. For example, a local bakery could publish a guide on choosing the right cake for a birthday party. A web design company could share tips on improving website speed. These topics can bring people to the business before they are ready to buy. Good content answers real customer questions and shows that you know your business. Over time, it can bring search traffic, build trust, generate leads, and support sales. For small businesses, content marketing can be a practical way to reach the right audience without relying only on paid advertising. Why Content Marketing Works for Small Businesses Small businesses cannot compete with large companies on advertising budgets. Content gives them another way to compete. Discoverability People use search engines, social networks, YouTube, Reddit, and other platforms when they need answers. Useful content can put your business in front of them while they are researching a problem. Trust A helpful article or video can show potential customers that you know your field. This can make a difference when they compare several businesses. Long-term Results A useful article can continue getting search traffic months after you publish it. A video can keep getting views. A guide can keep generating email subscribers. Results are not guaranteed, but good content has the chance to keep working after the initial publishing effort. Affordability You don’t need expensive cameras or a large content team. A phone, a computer, and your own knowledge can be enough for many content formats. Marketing Channels One good article can become a newsletter, several social posts, a short video, an infographic, and a checklist. That gives you more content without creating everything from scratch. Best Content Marketing Ideas for Small Businesses Here are practical ideas you can use across different industries. 1. Answer Common Customer Questions Start with the questions customers ask you again and again. Turn those questions into blog posts, videos, social posts, or email content. A plumber could answer: Why is my tap leaking? How often should I check my pipes? What causes low water pressure? A software company could explain: How does this feature work? Which plan should I choose? How do I solve this common problem? These topics are useful because they come directly from customer needs. 2. Create How-To Guides How-to content gives readers something they can use immediately. Break a task into simple steps. Add screenshots, photos, examples, or videos when they help. A coffee shop could publish a guide to different brewing methods. A photographer could explain how to prepare for a family photo session. You can make these guides short or detailed depending on the topic. 3. Publish Local Content Local businesses can use content to become more visible in their area. Write about local events, neighbourhoods, attractions, community activities, or problems related to your industry. For example, a pet shop could publish: “5 Dog-Friendly Parks in [City]” A restaurant could publish: “A Weekend Food Guide to [City]” This type of content can attract local readers who may become customers. 4. Create Short Videos You don’t need professional equipment to make useful videos. Use your phone to create short videos for Instagram, TikTok, YouTube Shorts, Facebook, or other platforms. Create videos with: Quick tips Product demonstrations Tutorials FAQs Behind-the-scenes clips Customer stories Before-and-after videos Keep each video focused on one idea. 5. Share Customer Stories Customer stories can show what your business does better than a sales pitch can. Ask customers if they are willing to share their experience. You could create a short interview, written story, or video. Explain the customer’s problem, how you helped, and what changed afterwards. Get permission before publishing personal information, photos, or videos. 6. Create Product Demo Videos Show people how your product works. Don’t just list features. Show the product solving a real problem . For example, a kitchen equipment store could demonstrate how a product works in a real kitchen. Keep the video focused. Answer the questions a customer would have before buying. 7. Create Infographics Infographics with quick tips make complex information easy to understand. They present valuable insights in a visual format that grabs attention. This type of content is a smart way for small businesses to educate customers and build backlinks. You could create: Statistics Checklists Step-by-step processes Comparisons Quick tips Industry facts Infographics work well on websites, blogs, and visual content platforms like Pinterest. They are easy to save and share. Soon, these visuals will expand your reach, improve engagement, and position your brand as helpful and resourceful. 8. Publish Seasonal Content Seasonal content keeps your content marketing fresh and relevant. People look for ideas, products, and tips that connect with holidays, seasons, and special events. Creating content around these times helps your business join the conversation and stay visible. Ideas include: Holiday buying guides Summer tips Back-to-school content Festival guides Seasonal maintenance advice Gift guides Local event content Publish seasonal content early enough for people to find and use it. You can use seasonal keywords, product guides, tips, and offers to attract timely traffic and encourage sales. 9. Start an Email Newsletter An email newsletter gives you a direct way to stay in touch with people who have shown interest in your business. Share useful tips instead of sending only sales messages. A bookstore could send: 5 books worth reading this month A fitness business could send: Three simple workouts you can do at home You can include product updates and offers, but useful information should remain a regular part of the newsletter. 10. Work With Local Creators Photo by Nhà văn Find local creators whose audience matches your target customers. Collaborate for product reviews, social media shoutouts, giveaways, or even co-hosted events. The key is to create partnerships that feel genuine and beneficial for both sides. A restaurant could work with a local food creator. A clothing shop could work with a local fashion creator. The creator doesn’t need millions of followers. A smaller audience that trusts the creator can be more useful than a large audience with little interest in your business. These collaborations increase your business’s visibility and credibility. When people see someone they trust supporting your business, they are more likely to check it out themselves. It’s a smart way to grow through community connections. 11. Answer Questions on Reddit, Quora and Communities People ask questions about products, services, problems, and industries every day. Find questions that match your expertise and give useful answers. But don’t turn every answer into an advertisement. On community platforms, your reputation matters. Give people a useful answer first. Link to your own content only when it adds something they need. 12. Show Behind-the-Scenes Content Behind-the-scenes content shows the human side of your business. It gives customers a look at what happens beyond the finished product. This type of content makes your brand feel more approachable and authentic. Show: How do you make a product How do you prepare an order Your workspace Your team A normal workday How do you prepare for an event How do you solve a customer problem Sharing such glimpses regularly helps customers feel closer to your brand and encourages them to support your business with pride. 13. Create Lead Magnets A lead magnet is a useful free resource that people can download in exchange for their email address. Create something that solves a specific customer problem, such as a checklist, ebook, guide, worksheet, or resource list. Examples include: Checklists Templates Ebooks Worksheets Guides Resource lists Planning sheets Free reports For example, an accounting firm could offer a small-business tax checklist. A useful lead magnet can help you grow your email list and generate potential customers. 14. Publish Case Studies Case studies show how you helped a real customer. A simple structure works well: Problem → Solution → Result Explain the situation, what you did, and what happened. Add real numbers when you have permission to share them. Case studies are especially useful for businesses selling services because potential customers can see what working with you may look like. 15. Create Free Templates Free templates can give your audience something useful while introducing them to your business. Create templates that solve common problems your customers face. You could create: Social media calendars Budget sheets Email templates Project templates Marketing plans Checklists Content briefs A free template can attract search traffic and generate email subscribers simultaneously. Let visitors download the template after entering their email address. This can help you build your email list while providing real value. 16. Make Checklists People love content that tells them what they need to do. Create checklists for common tasks related to your niche. Examples: Website launch checklist Moving checklist Home maintenance checklist SEO checklist Social media checklist New business checklist Keep the checklist practical. Don’t add items just to make it longer. 17. Host Webinars or Online Workshops A webinar can help you teach something while introducing people to your business. Possible topics include: Product training Beginner workshops Industry updates Q&A sessions Tutorials Expert discussions Record the session so you can reuse it later. One webinar can become a blog post, several short videos, social posts, and an email. 18. Interview Industry Experts Interview people who have useful knowledge. Ask them practical questions your audience wants answered. You can publish the interview as: A blog post A video A podcast A newsletter A social media series Expert interviews can add different viewpoints to your website. 19. Create Expert Roundups Ask several experts the same question and combine their answers into one article. For example: “15 SEO Experts Share Their Best Tip for Small Businesses” Contact the contributors when the article goes live. Some may share it with their own audience. 20. Publish Comparison Guides Comparison guides help people choose between products, services, or solutions. Compare the options based on price, features, pros, cons, and who each one suits. Examples: Product A vs. Product B Tool A vs. Tool B DIY vs. hiring a professional Different service plans Different product types Keep your comparison fair and explain the differences clearly. This type of content can attract people who are close to making a purchase. 21. Create Free Tools and Calculators Free tools can attract visitors and give them a reason to return to your website. Create a simple tool that solves a problem your customers often face. Ideas include: ROI calculators Budget calculators Savings calculators Pricing calculators Quiz tools Product finders Planning tools You can promote the tool through search, social media, and email to reach more potential customers. 22. Encourage User-Generated Content Ask customers to share photos, videos, reviews, or experiences. For example, a clothing store could encourage customers to share photos wearing its products. A restaurant could ask customers to tag the business in their food photos. But you should get permission before reusing customer content on your website or social media. 23. Build a Customer FAQ Hub Create a dedicated FAQ section that answers the questions customers ask most often. Cover questions about: Pricing Products Services Delivery Returns Setup Support Availability Google removed FAQ rich results from Search in 2026, so don’t create FAQs just to chase a special search result. They are still useful when they help real customers. You can use questions from customer emails, sales calls, reviews, and support chats. A useful FAQ hub saves customers time and helps them make decisions with less confusion. 24. Start a Podcast or Video Series A podcast or video series can help you share useful information regularly. Choose a topic your customers care about and cover one idea in each episode. For example: Small Business Marketing Tips — Episode 1 Small Business Marketing Tips — Episode 2 You can answer common questions, interview experts, share tips, or discuss industry news. Keep the format simple and consistent. You can turn each episode into blog posts, social media posts, or email content. 25. Create a Content Series Break a broad topic into a series of related posts instead of covering everything in one article. For example, a small business blog could create a series about SEO basics, with separate posts on keywords, on-page SEO, local SEO, and link building. Link the posts together so readers can easily find the next topic. A content series can keep readers coming back for more. This can make the site easier for readers to explore. 26. Publish Founder or Expert Content Share knowledge from the people who actually run the business. Talk about: Lessons learned Mistakes Industry changes Customer problems Business decisions Personal experiences Opinions based on experience A founder could share how the business started, while an expert could explain a complex topic in simple words. This type of content adds a personal voice to your website and gives readers a reason to trust your experience. 27. Publish Industry Trends Help customers understand changes in your industry. Explain what has changed, why it matters, and what they should do. Don’t simply repeat news from other websites. Add your own analysis or experience. Google says its systems aim to reward helpful, reliable, people-first content, including content that adds original information, research, or analysis. citeturn0search12 28. Create Resource Pages Create a page that brings useful resources about one topic together. Add links to your best guides, tools, checklists, videos, and related articles. For example: The Small Business SEO Resource Hub It could link to: Keyword research guides SEO tools Local SEO articles Technical SEO tutorials Link-building guides SEO checklists Keep the page organized and update it when you publish useful new resources. 29. Repurpose Your Best Content Get more value from content that already performs well. You can even combine several related posts into an ebook or guide. Turn one strong article into: Short videos Social posts An email An infographic A checklist A LinkedIn post A podcast episode Repurposing saves time and helps you reach people who prefer different content formats. Start with your most useful or popular content. 30. Create Content for Different Buying Stages Photo by Kaboompics from Pexels Not every visitor is ready to buy. Some are learning about a problem, while others are comparing options or looking for a product. Create content for each stage. For people who are just starting their research, publish beginner guides, tips, and answers to common questions. For those comparing options, create product comparisons, reviews, case studies, and detailed guides. For visitors ready to buy, offer product demos, pricing information, FAQs, and customer testimonials. You should create content for existing customers, too. Publish tutorials, setup guides, troubleshooting tips, and useful product updates. This approach helps you give people the right information at the right time and can guide them from their first visit toward a purchase. 31. Publish Original Research Original data can make your website more useful. You could survey your customers or collect data from your own business. Examples: Customer survey results Industry statistics Pricing research Product usage data Local market research Original research can give other websites a reason to mention and link to your work. 32. Create Content Around Common Mistakes Photo by RDNE Stock project from Pexels People want to know what they should avoid when trying something new. Use this to create useful content around common mistakes in your industry. Create articles such as: 10 Common Website Mistakes 7 SEO Mistakes Small Businesses Make 8 Email Marketing Mistakes 5 Mistakes to Avoid When Hiring a Freelancer Explain why each mistake causes problems and show readers what they can do instead. You can turn these topics into blog posts, videos, checklists, or social media posts. This content can attract people who are actively looking for solutions. It also shows that you understand the problems your customers face and know how to help them avoid costly mistakes. 33. Create “Best Of” Guides “Best of” guides help people compare several products, tools, or services before making a decision. Choose a topic that matches your customers and explain the options clearly. Examples: Best accounting tools for small businesses Best free website tools Best email marketing platforms Best productivity apps Best social media tools Include useful details such as key features, pricing, pros, cons, and who each option is suitable for. Keep your recommendations honest and explain how you selected them. These guides can attract people who are already researching a purchase. They can bring search traffic, build trust, and introduce readers to your products or services when there is a natural connection. 34. Create Content Upgrades A content upgrade is a useful bonus resource related to a specific blog post. It gives readers extra help without making the main article longer. For example, a post about creating a content calendar could offer a downloadable content calendar template. Keep the upgrade closely related to the article. This makes it more useful and can encourage readers to download it. You can ask for an email address before providing the resource if you want to grow your email list. Content upgrades can turn existing blog traffic into leads while giving readers something they can use right away. Content Marketing Examples for Small Businesses Photo by Jakub Zerdzicki Different businesses need different types of content. A good starting point is to choose a pillar topic and create several related pieces around it. This gives you more content ideas and helps you build useful topic clusters. Here are five examples from different industries. 1. Digital Marketing Agency Pillar topic: Digital Marketing for Small Businesses Supporting content ideas: How to Increase Website Traffic SEO Tips for Small Businesses Social Media Marketing Guide Email Marketing Ideas Content Marketing Strategy Best Digital Marketing Tools Example: Create a detailed guide called “Digital Marketing for Small Businesses: A Beginner’s Guide.” Link the supporting articles to this main guide. 2. Web Hosting Service Pillar topic: Web Hosting for Beginners Supporting content ideas: Shared Hosting vs. VPS Hosting Managed WordPress Hosting Guide How to Choose Web Hosting How to Move a Website to a New Host How to Improve Website Speed Common Web Hosting Mistakes Example: Publish “Complete Web Hosting Guide for Small Businesses.” Link related hosting guides to the main article and relevant hosting plans. 3. Travel Operator Pillar topic: Travel Guide to Tokyo Supporting content ideas: Best Places to Visit in Tokyo Tokyo 5-Day Travel Itinerary Best Time to Visit Japan Japan Travel Costs Best Beaches in Tokyo Japan Food Guide Example: Create “Complete Tokyo Travel Guide for First-Time Visitors.” Link destination guides and travel tips to the main guide. 4. Local Restaurant Pillar topic: Food Guide to [City] Supporting content ideas: Best Local Dishes to Try Popular Food Spots in [City] Local Food Festivals Restaurant Guide for Families Vegetarian Food Guide Behind-the-Scenes Restaurant Stories Example: Publish “Complete Food Guide to [City].” Link related food articles and restaurant content back to the main guide. 5. Online Software Business Pillar topic: Social Media Management Supporting content ideas: How to Schedule Social Media Posts Social Media Content Calendar Best Times to Post on Social Media Social Media Analytics Guide How to Repurpose Social Media Content Social Media Scheduling Tips Example: Create “Complete Social Media Management Guide for Small Businesses.” Link tutorials, tips, and product guides to the main article. These examples show how one broad topic can become a group of connected articles. This approach gives your audience more useful information and creates a clear internal linking structure for your website. useful articles and other content around smaller questions. You might also be interested in these posts: 130+ Easy Social Media Post Ideas to Keep Your Feed Fresh SEO vs Social Media Marketing: Which Is Better for Your Business? How to Increase Blog Traffic: 19 Proven Ways to Get More Visitors How to Create a Content Marketing Strategy A list of ideas is useful, but you need a simple system to turn those ideas into results. 1. Set a Business Goal Start by deciding what you want your content to achieve. A clear goal helps you choose the right topics and measure your progress. You may want more website traffic, leads, email subscribers, sales, or local customers. It could be: More organic traffic More leads More sales More email subscribers More local customers More product enquiries Choose one or two main goals instead of trying to achieve everything at once. Set a simple target and give yourself a time frame. This makes it easier to see whether your content marketing efforts are working. 2. Know Your Audience Learn who you want to reach before creating content. Find out what your customers need, what questions they ask, and what problems they face. Look at customer reviews, support messages, sales conversations, and comments on social media for useful clues. Find out: Who buys from you? What problems do they have? What questions do they ask? What products do they compare? What stops them from buying? Which websites and platforms do they use? Create a simple customer profile with details such as their needs, interests, goals, and buying habits. This helps you choose topics that matter to them. Use the same words your customers use when describing their problems. Clear, familiar language can make your content easier to understand and more useful. 3. Find Customer Questions Your customers can give you many useful content ideas. Start with the questions they ask before, during, and after a purchase. Check customer emails, support chats, reviews, sales calls, and social media comments. Look through: Google autocomplete Google Search Console Reddit Quora Customer emails Support conversations Sales calls Reviews Competitor websites You can use keyword tools such as Semrush to find related searches and assess opportunities. The goal isn’t to collect hundreds of keywords. Find topics that match your customers and your business. Answer these questions through blog posts, videos, guides, or FAQs. This keeps your content focused on real problems instead of random topics. 4. Choose Content Pillars Pick three to five broad subjects that your business wants to be known for. For a small SEO agency, the pillars could be: SEO Content marketing Local SEO Website traffic Marketing tools Then create supporting articles around each pillar. 5. Build Topic Clusters A topic cluster connects a main guide with related supporting content. For example: Main guide: Content Marketing for Small Businesses Supporting articles: Content marketing ideas Content marketing strategy Content calendar Content marketing tools Content marketing examples Content repurposing Content marketing ROI Local content marketing Content marketing mistakes Link these articles to each other where useful. 6. Create a Content Calendar A content calendar helps you plan what to publish and when to publish it. List your topics, content types, publishing dates, and promotion channels in one place. You can use a spreadsheet, calendar app, or project management tool. For example: 1 detailed blog post each week 2–3 social posts from each article 1 newsletter each week or month 1 short video each week Plan content around your main topics, seasonal events, product launches, and customer needs. Leave some room for timely topics that come up during the year. A simple calendar can prevent last-minute writing and help you publish regularly. It also makes it easier to see whether your content covers different topics and reaches different parts of your audience. If you’re struggling to fill your calendar, these methods can help you generate blog post ideas based on popular topics and related searches 7. Write for People First Don’t write an article simply because a keyword has search volume. Ask: Would my target customer find this useful? Google’s current guidance recommends people-first content and warns against creating large amounts of content mainly to attract search traffic. 8. Add Original Experience Your own experience can make content more useful and different from similar articles online. Share real examples, lessons, customer questions, test results, screenshots, or mistakes you have seen. Add: Your own examples Customer questions Screenshots Data Tests Lessons Expert opinions Real experiences Don’t repeat information that readers can find everywhere. Add details from your own work whenever possible. This gives readers practical information and helps show that your business has real knowledge of the topic. 9. Add a Next Step Give readers a clear action to take after they finish your content. The next step should match the topic and their needs. You could link to a related article, offer a free template, invite them to join your email list, or ask them to contact your business. For example: Read next: How to Create a Content Calendar Or: Download: Free Content Calendar Template Or: Need help? Contact us for a consultation. A relevant next step keeps readers on your website and can turn useful content into leads or sales. How AI Can Help With Content Marketing in 2026 AI tools can speed up parts of the content process. You can use them to: Brainstorm topics Group keywords Create content outlines Find questions to answer Turn an article into social posts Summarize research Suggest headline ideas Find gaps in an existing article Create first drafts of simple content But don’t publish large amounts of AI-generated content without adding your own value. Google says generative AI can be useful for research and structure, but generating many pages without adding value can fall under its scaled content abuse policy . Use AI to speed up your workflow. Add your own experience, examples, research, opinions, and editing. Content Marketing and Google AI Search Google now includes AI features such as AI Overviews and AI Mode in Search. That doesn’t mean you need a completely different SEO strategy. Google’s own guidance says the basic SEO principles still apply to AI search features. Google recommends helpful, reliable, people-first content and says there are no special technical requirements just for appearing in AI Overviews or AI Mode. For small businesses, that means you should focus on: Answering questions clearly Using useful headings Providing original information Showing first-hand experience Keeping business information accurate Adding relevant local information Using useful images and videos Building a strong website structure Don’t write content just to appear in an AI answer. Write content that gives people a reason to visit your website in the first place. Final Thoughts Content marketing doesn’t have to mean publishing a new blog post every day. Start with the questions your customers already ask. Turn those questions into useful articles, videos, emails, guides, checklists, and other content. Then connect those pieces. Create a main topic. Build supporting articles around it. Link related pages together. Repurpose your best work. Promote it where your customers spend time. Track leads and sales, not just page views. You don’t need a huge marketing budget. You need useful ideas, a clear plan, and a publishing schedule you can actually maintain. Start with three or four ideas from this list. See what your audience responds to. Then build from there. FAQ What are the best content marketing ideas for small businesses? Start with customer questions, how-to guides, local content, short videos, case studies, email newsletters, checklists, free resources, product demonstrations, and customer stories. How can a small business do content marketing with a small budget? Start with content you can create using your existing knowledge and equipment. Blog posts, FAQs, short videos, email newsletters, customer stories, and social posts can be created without a large budget. How often should a small business publish content? There is no perfect publishing frequency. Choose a schedule you can maintain while keeping the content useful. One strong article every week can be more useful than several weak posts. How long does content marketing take to work? It depends on the topic, website, competition, content quality, distribution, and audience. Some content can attract attention quickly, while search-focused content may take much longer. Is content marketing better than paid advertising? They serve different purposes. Paid advertising can bring traffic quickly. Content marketing can build an asset that continues to attract visitors and leads over time. Many businesses can use both. What type of content works best for small businesses? There is no single format that works for every business. Start with the questions and problems your customers have. Then choose the format that explains the answer best. Can AI help with content marketing? Yes. AI can help with research, brainstorming, outlining, repurposing, and other tasks. Review and improve AI-assisted content before publishing it. As a small business owner, your content is one of your most important assets. This allows you to speak directly to your audience or reach new customers and market your goods and services. Today there are many ways for small businesses to create and distribute content. You might share insights on your business social media platforms , start a blog , or launch an email newsletter. The content you create and how you share it is part of your content marketing strategy. Content marketing isn't explicitly sales-oriented, but offers original ideas that provide value and show your expertise. A content marketing strategy is more than just a schedule of when to post something. Through text, videos, and photos, you can convey your values and brand and what makes your business special. Here's how to develop and execute a content strategy tailored to your unique business and goals, and then adjust it as needed over time. Start With A Website Trial What is a content marketing strategy? A content marketing strategy is a blueprint for the content you create for your business and how to distribute it. This strategy should align with and complement the goals of your overall business strategy . Content marketing strategy for a small business requires you to consider multiple factors, including: Your goals: Content plans will differ depending on your goals. A hair stylist who wants more customers might want to create photo-heavy social media posts that show their client work, while a marketer who wants more speaking engagements might create content that demonstrates their expertise. Your audience: This identifies who you’re trying to reach with your content. It should align with your brand’s ideal audience or customer. Audiences can vary from channel to channel. Kinds of content you're creating: In your strategy, go into detail about specific content types. Common ones include photo essays, behind-the-scenes videos, or blogs about your process. No matter what you choose, make sure this is high-quality content . Distribution channels: There are many ways to distribute content, including via email, social media, and your website. A content strategy addresses which channels you plan to use and what kind of content you'll share on them. Schedule of content: A content calendar is a vital part of your content strategy. This is a detailed outline of when and where you plan on sharing your content. How to measure success: Once you settle on what kind of content to create, you can determine which metrics to track. Growing businesses might track milestones like number of customers or sales increases. Content creators might measure video views or engagement. Entrepreneurs frequently develop a content strategy for a specific channel—for example, an email newsletter or a specific social media platform—as well as a broader content strategy for their business. Types of content in content marketing There's no one right way to do content marketing. You can focus on one type of content or produce a mix of content and space it out over time. For example, you might post on social media daily but share a video only once a month. Content falls into a few main categories, including: Written content : Articles based on interviews with subject matter experts, case studies about successful customers, blogs detailing insights into work you've produced or targeting SEO keywords , newsletters about topics related to your business Video: Behind-the-scenes or process clips, an explainer video demonstrating your expertise in a certain area, a montage of business-related photos set to music Photographs/graphics: Infographics, a photo essay of an event, photo storytelling alongside an article Social media content: A photo with a long caption, a photo carousel with text overlaid from a story, demo or recap videos, user-generated content Podcasts: Interviews , Q&As, shorter conversations that can be repurposed for video You can often cross-post content across multiple marketing channels. For example, you might distribute a podcast as a video as well as audio, or post snippets of your interview on social media. Repurposing content is another smart strategy. A case study or article can be excerpted on graphics and shared as a photo carousel or turned into a video script. Tools like Unfold make it easy to create social media content. Do you need a content marketing strategy? Even if you start with one type of content or marketing channel, content marketing offers an invaluable opportunity to direct the narrative around your business and raise awareness of your brand. A content marketing strategy offers multiple benefits to growing businesses. It helps you stay organized. As a busy business owner, it can be easy to lose track of the content you have or want to share. And planning content on the fly is difficult. A content marketing strategy offers a detailed framework to maintain consistency. You can build your brand. Original content is an excellent way to communicate your values and mission . Both of these things are part of your brand and inform how people view your business. Identify new audiences or business opportunities. It's not uncommon for businesses to discover new potential revenue streams when making content marketing plans. For example, you might uncover a need your audience has or discover a new audience altogether. You can establish yourself as a thought leader. Creating thoughtful content lets you share your expertise. Being known as a thought leader can open up other ways to promote or grow your business, such as guest posts, podcast appearances, courses , or live events. Get Started 9 steps to create a content marketing strategy Developing a content marketing strategy can feel like a big undertaking. But you’re probably already sharing some content. A strategy is just a way to attach goals and systems to the process. Breaking it down into individual steps can make defining and reaching your goals more manageable. Set your goals. These should be specific to the content you're planning to produce, and reflect both short-term and long-term goals . Focus on what feels achievable and in line with your business goals. You can add or subtract once you start posting content. Identify your audience. Determining who you’re communicating with will guide your content. For example, your audience might respond better to short text posts or videos rather than lengthy blogs. The part of your audience you’re speaking to also matters. For potential customers, you might want to create content that speaks more about your business offerings or unique expertise. Determine your areas of focus. Your content should be in a niche that speaks most directly to your areas of expertise. If you're an editor, you might offer writing tips, while a wedding photographer might discuss how best to capture various moments of the day. Becoming known as an expert in a specific area can help your business grow. Choose content types and topics. Focus on doing one or two kinds of content well. You can always scale up if you have the capacity to take on more. The topics should align with your niches and goals. Content that feels random or like it strays from your core brand can confuse audiences. Set metrics to track. The content and goals you focus on will dictate the metrics you track. If you're focusing on audience engagement, time spent watching a video clip is a key indicator. Success for a blog might mean pageviews or shares. Decide distribution methods. Determine the channel that makes sense for your business. If you're a writer, a text-based newsletter might make sense, while graphic designers will likely want a visual-heavy platform. Create a content calendar. Releasing content on a steady basis is crucial. This keeps your business top of mind for potential customers and opens opportunities to attract new ones. A calendar will help you stay on track with content production and sharing. Start creating content. Now it's time to share your knowledge and expertise with your audience. Consider creating a month or two of content in advance, so you're not scrambling to fill slots at the last minute. This is a common practice with content that takes longer to produce, such as podcasts or videos. Measure success. Once you've started sharing content and gathering reactions, you can adjust your strategy accordingly. Set aside weekly and monthly time to review your goals and metrics. How are you tracking over time? Do any of your goals or metrics need to be adjusted or changed? Perhaps you realize that the pace of content creation isn't realistic, or your audience isn't watching videos. How to engage with your content’s audience Communication is a two-way street, and people will relate to your brand and business if they feel as though they’re part of a community. Consider creating content that gives you space to connect with your audience personally, or setting aside time to respond to comments. Hold a live Q&A. Many social media channels make it easy to go live on video and take follower questions. Be sure to advertise this session in advance so people know when to arrive or send questions in advance. Comment on your social media posts. This is one of the easiest ways to engage with your audience. Your comments don't have to be extensive. For example, if someone shares your post or left a comment, simply respond by saying "Thank you!" along with an emoji. Share posts by other people. Another easy way to engage with your audience is to share the content they produce on your own channels. Adding your own comment or insight along with a share deepens your expertise and can also help build community. Offer exclusive content. Rewarding your loyal followers with exclusives. This could be a subscriber-only chat or newsletter. If you sell goods or services, sharing an occasional discount or coupon is also a nice gesture. Tips for content engagement Engaging with your audience is about building a positive association with you and your brand. Find ways to make the experience feel fun and natural—your enjoyment will come through in your tone. Focus on one or two channels. Content engagement is more time-consuming than you might think. Focus your time on the channels most relevant to your business and community. Be authentic. Although your content might be on behalf of a business, be personable and genuine. Content marketing is meant to be a soft sales tool by design, so try and stay away from jargon. Keep your tone neutral-to-positive. Not every comment on your content is going to be positive. This can sting, but try not to take it personally. If you decide to respond, avoid being accusatory or defensive. Acknowledge what the commenter said and engage with them thoughtfully. Remember, content strategy and growth is a marathon, not a sprint. You'll risk stress or burnout if you try to create or share too much content at once. Do what you can with the time you have.
